messages:
anya: Quick Q from a trip to Munich last week. Had a bad allergic reaction to a meal on the first night and needed to see a local urgent care. Paid 85 for the clinic visit and 22 for meds at a pharmacy. I don't have an itemized clinic invoice, only a payment receipt that shows 'medical services' and a small handwritten note from the clinic. Can we reimburse medical expenses incurred during business travel? cc @travel-ops

rob: Sorry you had to deal with that! Short answer: medically necessary expenses incurred while on a business trip are reimbursable when documented. We require receipts; if the vendor can't provide an itemized invoice, manager-signed attestation + the clinic receipt may be accepted.

emily: Finance checklist: 1) Upload clinic receipt + pharmacy receipt. 2) If the clinic only provides a generic payment slip, request a brief invoice mentioning service date and diagnosis code if possible. 3) Add a short note in Expensify: "medical - allergic reaction - 2026-06-11" and tag your manager for approval.

anya: The clinic was a tiny walk-in and said they don't print invoices beyond the payment slip. Is a manager attestation enough? Also travel insurance said to file with them first  do we need to involve travel insurance?

travel-ops: Policy excerpt: "Employees should attempt to file eligible medical claims with the company's travel insurance first. If travel insurance pays, the company will not reimburse duplicate amounts. If insurance denies or is unavailable, submit expenses to finance with supporting docs and manager approval."

rob: Practically: 1) Scan and upload what you have (payment slip + pharmacy receipt). 2) Open a travel-insurance claim (we can help) and attach the docs. 3) If insurance is slow or denies, submit to finance with a manager attestation indicating the treatment was business-related and unavoidable. Finance will coordinate offsets if insurance reimburses later.

anya: I opened the insurer ticket (INS-6221) but they asked for a physician note; clinic said they can email a short note for 15. Will that help?

emily: Yes, a short clinic note confirming date/treatment increases chances. If the clinic emails it, attach to the insurer and to your Expensify expense. Add a privacy note: redact sensitive health details if you prefer; a simple statement of treatment + date is fine.

anya: What about missing taxi receipt from the ride to the clinic? I paid cash 6 and the driver didn't give a receipt. Can I claim that too?

finance-bot: Policy: "Lost or missing receipts for small, necessary travel expenses (taxi, tips, small meds) may be attested with manager approval up to 50 per item. For medical incidents, we accept reasonable attestation if accompanied by clinic documentation and manager sign-off."

rob: So for the cash taxi: add a 'lost receipt attestation' in Expensify, note amount, date/time and route (hotel -> clinic). Ask your manager to sign the attestation. That should be enough to approve up to the policy limit.

anya: Great. One more: I also bought an over-the-counter antihistamine for 9 and the pharmacy receipt is just a single line total. Is that reimbursable?

emily: OTC meds related to an acute illness on a business trip are reimbursable if reasonable. Attach the pharmacy receipt and annotate the line (e.g., "cetirizine - 10 tablets"). If the receipt is generic, add a short note explaining the item.

travel-ops: Reminder: if the medical claim is substantial, contact People Ops before travel in the future and consider pre-trip medical coverage notes or carrying an insurer card. For anything that looks like non-urgent elective care, get pre-approval.

anya: Thanks all 60a I'll upload the clinic note + receipts and start the insurer claim. Tagging my manager now. Appreciate the quick guidance! :pray:
